utilities.name: Énergir

sources.description: Pricing page that links the current Conditions of Service and Tariff edition

Conditions of Service and Tariff as of October 1, 2026: supply, transportation, load balancing, Rate D1, renewable-gas socialization and cap-and-trade prices (link is rediscovered from the pricing page each run)

utilities.notes: Énergir (formerly Gaz Métro) is the principal natural gas distributor in Quebec. Regulated by the Régie de l'énergie du Québec. Default Rate D1 is parsed live for residential and business listings: seven annual-volume basic-fee bands, nine daily distribution blocks, supply, transportation, conditional load balancing and renewable-gas socialization, and the cap-and-trade (CTEAS) price, all in native cents/m3 stored as $/m3. Rates D3 and D4 (subscribed-volume minimum daily obligation bands, withdrawal prices, eligibility thresholds) are parsed from article 14.3 of the same tariff. Interruptible D5, the load-factor balancing formula, rate reductions and fixed-price/renewable supply options remain gaps. Batch 8 audited inventory-related adjustments (Energir inventory fact sheet): they are customer-specific supply/transportation price-difference adjustments or credits computed from each customer's storage parameters, with no published unit price, so they are documented conditions and are never added as a component. Batch 9 adds interruptible Rate D5 (PDF pages 62-65; Category A/B load-balancing alternatives conditional) and the dated RNG supply price (page 38) as an optional replacement component on D1/D3/D4/D5. Fixed-price supply is supplier-specific and unpriced.

Approved gas tariff index; required evidence that Rate 2 small and Rate 3 large commercial service is available in the Municipality of Revelstoke

utilities.notes: FortisBC Energy is the natural gas distribution arm of FortisBC, serving most of British Columbia. Regulated by the British Columbia Utilities Commission (BCUC). Rates 1/2/3 are parsed live for Mainland/Vancouver Island and Fort Nelson with daily basic charges and $/GJ delivery, storage and transport and cost of gas; Rate 5 (monthly basic, $/GJ/month daily-demand charge, riders) and Rate 4 seasonal (off-peak/extension periods) are parsed from their approved rate schedules for Mainland/Vancouver Island. Missing carbon evidence rejects live output. Fort Nelson Rates 4/5 (no published price table), Revelstoke propane, Rates 6/7 and Customer Choice marketer prices remain gaps. Batch 7 adds Residential Rate 1 Revelstoke propane (9 live total) from the residential page table, with its own motor-fuel-tax carbon evidence. Rates 6/7 and industrial service are excluded. Batch 8 adds Commercial Rates 2/3 Revelstoke propane (11 live total): the business-page Revelstoke tables are accepted only when the approved tariff index authorizes each class in Revelstoke and the residential page confirms propane service; each class fails independently. Batch 10 adds Rate 7 General Interruptible Service (monthly basic as printed; curtailment-limited delivery; Sumas-indexed overrun as a condition) and delivery-only transportation Rates 22/23/25/27 (16 live). Rate 7 PDF links are rediscovered from the business page and Rate 22-27 PDFs from the approved tariff index; marketer commodity is excluded, Rate 22 firm/interruptible charges are conditional, and Rates 6/6P/26 NGV and 22A/22B shipper-specific service are excluded. Fort Nelson 4/5/7/22-27 have no price table. Batch 11 adds Customer Choice 1U/2U/3U (delivery-only, marketer commodity excluded; not offered in Fort Nelson) and RNG 1RNG/2RNG/3RNG/5RNG/7RNG for Mainland/Vancouver Island plus 1RNG/2RNG/3RNG Fort Nelson (27 live); the RNG Charge replaces Cost of Gas only on the customer-chosen share, so both commodity charges are conditional and no blend is computed. Variant PDFs (rateschedule_1u/2u/3u/1b/2b/3b/5b/7b) are rediscovered from the tariff index. RNG Blend Service percentage is unpublished; 11RNG (short-term sale to transportation customers) and 3VRNG/5VRNG (vehicles) are excluded.

sources.description: Current residential Centra gas basic, commodity and delivery components

Dated federal zero fuel-charge applicability naming Manitoba; required for complete carbon evidence

utilities.notes: Twelve current residential/commercial Sales, T-service and marketer-supply variants. Source cents/m3 are normalized to dollars/m3, without heat-content conversion; native volumetric demand units and component dates are preserved. Delivery/demand totals are checked against their parts, not added twice. Private marketer commodity is excluded and explicit carbon evidence is mandatory. Batch 8 requires the PUB-approved schedule (Order 138/25) for class annual-volume boundaries, one-year elections/contracts, Mainline pressure, winter-month billing demand, T-service 200 GJ/day nomination and interruptible alternate-supply pass-through conditions; missing schedule context rejects only the affected classes. Fixed-term commodity contracts are noted as a separate optional product, not priced. Batch 10 audits the schedule class list (PDF p.17) and commercial options on each run: Special Contract (single negotiated customer) and Power Station (generation fuel) are excluded with schedule evidence (p.20); Mainline Interruptible Sales (firm delivery) is built in batch 11 from a reviewed transcription of scanned Appendix A page 82 (page 80 also checked), live at medium confidence only while both page-image SHA-256 hashes, the Board Order/date headers and text cross-checks match (13 live); no T-Service variant because Mainline customers may only take firm transportation. No full catalogue-completion claim.

sources.description: Residential tiered (Step 1/Step 2) electricity rates sub-page

utilities.notes: BCUC-regulated residential choices include tiered 1101, flat 1151, each with optional 2101 time-of-day, plus closed dual-fuel 1105. The live parser reads the approved PDF including dates, separate 1901/1904 riders and conditional transformer discounts; the riders exclude 2101 adjustments. Business Rates 1300/1500/1600 are rebuilt from approved tariff pages 97-107 with separate RS1901/1904 riders and conditional primary-voltage/transformation discounts, plus Terms and Conditions Section 11 standard service charges. Batch 9 adds Transmission Service RS1830 (PDF pages 138-140) and closed RS1289 net-metering generation credit as a conditional adjustment (pages 223-231); batch 10 adds transmission pilots 2801/2802/2821/2822 (pages 187-216, conditional enrollment alternatives to RS1830, ending March 31, 2030) and conditional generation credits RS2289/2290 (pages 234-248) for 17 live; RS1892 freshet energy is Mid-C index priced and deferred with market-rate work, RS1828 is excluded (biomass contract), and irrigation, lighting, EV, IPP and standby-only service are excluded. Batch 8 adds the Terms and Conditions section 7.2 power-factor surcharge (PDF pages 53-54) to each business record as ten conditional bands in the source unit 'fraction of Rate section charges' (lagging power factor below 90%; nil at 90% or more; no leading-power-factor charge); a missing or malformed clause rejects business records only.

utilities.notes: Nine live records include D/DP/DM/DN/DT/Flex D, the closed Winter Credit adjustment and G/M. DT switches on source-defined outdoor temperature zones, not hourly TOU, and excludes off-grid service. Flex D preserves seasonal tiers, notified events and mutually exclusive product eligibility. Winter Credit is a conditional adjustment to Rate D, retaining reference-energy rules and enrollment cutoff. Multiplier, minimum-bill and demand rules remain conditions, not calculated bills. Inukjuak, net metering and remaining building business options still need audit; no full catalogue-completion claim. Batch 7 adds 11 live building options (20 live total): Inukjuak DN, Rate G9, Flex G/M/G9, three dual-energy rates, Winter Credit G and net-metering options I/III (option III keeps its own conditions). All components carry source URL, page detail and effective date. Industrial MA is not in the current edition; GD (backup), BR (EV), LD/LP (auxiliary/standby) are excluded. Batch 8 adds Net Metering Option I for Rate M (21 live total): Rate M application 4.28 (self-generation up to 1,000 kW) plus the shared Option I surplus-bank reset credit as a conditional $/kWh credit; Rate M charges stay separate. Batch 9 adds large-power Rates L (pages 63-66), LG (67-69) and H (71) with conditional voltage credits, plus the business Demand Response Leeway Option (pages 94-98) as alternative conditional credits (25 live). Batch 10 adds the business Demand Response Commitment Option (articles 6.13-6.36, PDF pages 83-93; 20 mutually exclusive sub-options, multi-year/short-notice credits and capped overrun deductions, all conditional adjustments to G/M/L/LG; 26 live). Rate F/FP (unmetered) is excluded; Load Retention, Additional Electricity (monthly announced price), closed Economic Development and Industrial Revitalization rates are not general published building prices.

sources.description: Residential electricity rates including basic charge and energy charge
Commercial and industrial electricity rates
Approved Electric Rate Schedule (January 1, 2026, PUB Order 1/26); Limited Use of Billing Demand tariffs 2026-50 to 2026-55

utilities.notes: Manitoba Hydro is a Crown corporation providing electricity in Manitoba. Electricity rates are among the lowest in Canada due to abundant hydroelectric generation. Regulated by the Manitoba Public Utilities Board (PUB). Twelve live January 2026 building records: residential standard, seasonal and diesel (basic charge also published for service over 200 A), plus general service small/medium/large/seasonal and diesel general service and diesel government/First Nation education. Large general-service voltage tiers cover building-related industrial service. Batch 10 adds six Limited Use of Billing Demand options 2026-50 to 2026-55 from the approved schedule as conditional alternatives that replace standard General Service charges (18 live); a schedule failure keeps the page classes and vice versa. Curtailable and surplus-energy programs publish no complete dated price; the net-billing credit lacks a published start date; standard service charges are not in the approved schedule and the $150 reconnection fee is undated. A failed residential or commercial page no longer discards the other page's live classes. Lighting is excluded.
